# Questions for the client

These confirmations would let me close the open items flagged in `STATUS.md`. The return as
prepared stands on the assumptions stated; answers may change the figures noted.

1. **Leo 2025 claim.** The 2019 order gives odd years to the father. Please confirm (a) the father
   (Leo's other parent) is actually claiming Leo for 2025, and (b) Elena will sign Form 8332 for
   2025. If the other parent will *not* claim Leo, tell us — the Reyses could then claim him
   (+$2,200 CTC) and the Form 8962 family size/FPL analysis changes materially.
2. **Prior-year S-corp records.** Do 2021–2024 K-1s (or prior Forms 7203) exist anywhere? Our
   $11,500 opening basis comes only from Marcus's note. Any correction moves the
   allowed/suspended split of the 2025 loss dollar-for-dollar.
3. **Brooklyn lease.** Please send the current lease (2019 term + renewals). Is $1,500/mo the
   contract rent with no escalator the landlord failed to apply, and is the tenant unrelated with
   no family/free-use arrangement? If the rent was reduced as a personal courtesy, the entire
   $19,550 rental deduction disappears (personal-use rule).
4. **Remote work facts (NY).** Did either employer have a New York office available that the
   Reyeses chose not to use? Any written remote-work agreement? Under NY's convenience-of-the-
   employer rule this decides whether July–December wages stay NY source (our current answer:
   yes, all $122,000 stays NY source).
5. **NY return.** The library has no NY rate schedule, so we did not compute NY tax or the IT-203
   refund. NY withholding was $6,752 — do you want the NY return prepared when authority is
   available, and please confirm no other NY items (e.g., 2024 NY carryovers).
